contribution.position: My reliability position is unchanged. The QA turn cites the perf report for a p99 of 180ms, but the perf report artifact records p99 at 410ms at peak load against a 250ms budget. That is the figure I am relying on, and the two readings need reconciling before the 'risk is contained' claim can stand. The incident log shows two sev2 incidents last quarter, both traced to retry storms. Latency over budget is a plausible trigger for that failure mode. The cost and runbook points are not in dispute on this axis. A documented rollback path limits recovery time but does not prevent a retry storm. The passing test report (412 passed, 0 failed) covers functional behavior, not peak-load behavior. Still needed: (a) which run produced 180ms versus 410ms, and whether either reflects the changed code path rather than the test environment; (b) the client retry and backoff configuration, and whether it is bounded at the measured latency; (c) a repeat load test with p99 inside budget, or an approved, documented exception.
